questions.question: Buckminsterfullerene is a nanoparticle characterised by spherical geometry and a hollow interior which contains how many carbon atoms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**60**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **60 carbon atoms** are organized in interlocking **hexagonal and pentagonal rings** to form the spherical molecule known as **buckminsterfullerene.**
 
• The spherical carbon allotrope known as a **buckminsterfullerene (C60) **has 60 atoms arranged in pentagons and hexagons, giving it a soccer ball-like form.
 
• A type of fullerene with the chemical formula C60 is buckminsterfullerene. It is shaped like a football and has a fused-ring construction that resembles a cage.** It is made up of twenty hexagons and twelve pentagons**. Its 60 carbon atoms are all linked to three of their neighbours.
 
• Each carbon atom generates three sigma bonds with three other carbon atoms in the fullerene's **sp2 hybridization state**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Carbon fullerene molecules can take on a variety of **geometries**, including tubes, spheres, cubes, and other pure solids comprised of just one type of atom. A feature of fullerenes is their hollow core, which is an area of empty space inside the molecule.
 
• Consider a basketball; it has a** spherical, leather outside**, but a hollow interior where air is trapped to give it its **bouncing motion**. With a fullerene, the situation is identical. It is entirely composed of carbon, and the interior of the structure is always hollow.
 
• HIV proteases' hydrophobic cavity can accommodate fullerene, which prevents substrates from reaching the** enzyme's catalytic site**. It has **antioxidant** and **radical scavenger properties**. Fullerene can also produce significant quantum yields of singlet oxygen when exposed to light.

questions.question: Total deposits with Post Office savings organisations are included in which money supply aggregate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**M4**__.

__
 
• The** Reserve Bank of India releases data for M1, M2, M3, and M4**—four different measurements of the money supply.
 
• The Post Office Savings are thus only included in M2 and M4.
 
• The **Post Office Savings Account (SB)** is comparable to any savings account offered by a retail bank.
 
• The minimum deposit amount is $500 and the minimum withdrawal amount is just $50. It offers a** 4% interest rate**.
 
• A savings bank account can be opened by both adults and minors.
 
• The** M2 **measurement of the money supply in India includes the savings deposits of post office savings banks, which gives it a bit more rigidity than the M1 measurement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• M1, M2, M3, and M4 were the four monetary aggregates that the RBI used to calculate the money supply between **1977 and 1998**.
 
• The idea of Reserve Money was also utilised by the central bank.
 
• In India, the post office offers a deposit programme called the **post office savings account**. 
 
• To calculate and gauge the total supply of money in the market, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** divides currency into four major categories, sometimes referred to as monetary aggregates.** M0, M1, M2, and M4 are the numbers.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the Indian Constitution as a Fundamental Duty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To respect elders**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A citizen of India has no inherent obligation to **amass property.**
 
• According to the Indian Constitution, following traffic laws is not a Basic Responsibility.
 
• **Article 51A of Part IV-A **of the Indian Constitution lists the fundamental obligations of Indian citizens.
 
 
• Respect the national flag, national anthem, and Indian Constitution as well as all of its ideas and institutions.
 
• To uphold and adhere to the lofty values that sparked the country's fight for freedom.
 
• To safeguard and defend India's **sovereignty, unification, and integrity.​**​
 
 
 
• The** moral responsibility** of all people to support the unity of India and advance patriotism are known as the **Basic Obligations**.
 
• These obligations, which are outlined in Section IV-A of the Constitution, affect both people and the country.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ​10 Basic Responsibilities were introduced to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
 
• Later, the 11th Basic Responsibility was included in the list by the 86th Amendment Act of 2002.
 
• In 1976, the **Swaran Singh Committee** proposed Basic Responsibilities.​
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee also advocated for the obligation to pay taxes. Yet, the Constitution did not include it.
 
• The** Constitution's Article 51A **lists the essential obligations.
 
• The **Basic Rights**, **Directive Principles of State Policy**, and** Fundamental Duties **are portions of the Indian Constitution that outline the fundamental duties and **rights of citizens** towards the state as well as the fundamental obligations of states to their inhabitants. 
 
• These articles are regarded as essential parts of the constitution, which was created during 1949 by the **Indian Constituent Assembly**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The sheet lava flows that follow may be extruded from rifts or linear fissures, massive volcanic eruptions, or many vents that are **reminiscent of the prehistoric epoch** when large flood basalts were formed.

• **Laterite soil: **
 
 
• **​**Both laterite and laterite rocks are frequently used **interchangeably**.
 
• There have been suggestions for the name to be completely dropped due to this as well as **more variance **in the ways that laterite is conceptualized (such as also as a **whole weathering profile** or theory about weathering).
 
• At least a few regolith development experts have thought that the name has become the subject of hopeless misunderstanding. There is a lot of material that resembles** Indian laterite** all around the world.
 
 
 
• **Alluvial soil: **
 
 
• **​**The other soil-forming elements affect the **final soil qualities as alluvial soils mature over time**.
 
• Alluvial soils frequently comprise layers of alluvium that were deposited consecutively and/or in fining-upward processes, making them **highly stratified**.
 
• Every time there is flooding, new alluvium is deposited on the soil in active **floodplains**.
 
• Each event will drop a different amount of alluvium.
 
• The rate at which small amounts of material are deposited on the soil can be scarcely noticeable and quickly assimilated into the underlying surface horizon relies on the temperature and biota.
 
• Subsequent soils can be totally buried by **additional alluvium** in larger quantities.
 
 
 
• **Red soil: **
 
 
• **​**About **13% **of the soils on Earth are red soil, a type of soil that often forms in warm, temperate, and humid areas.
 
• On top of a red layer of alluvium, it has **thin organic and organic-mineral layers of heavily leached soil**.
 
• Large levels of clay are typically present in red soils, which are typically the result of **old crystalline and metamorphic rock** weathering. Because of their **high iron concentration**, they have a deep red colour that can range from reddish brown to reddish yellow, hence their name.
 
• Depending on how it is handled, red soil can be either** good or terrible for growing **anything.

• Fertilizers and explosives frequently contain nitrates as a component. 
 
• About all **inorganic nitrates are water soluble**.
 
• Bismuth oxynitrate is an illustration of an insoluble nitrate.
 
 
 
• **NO2**:** **
 
 
• **​**The chemical compound with the formula** NO is nitrogen dioxide**.

 It belongs to a group of nitrogen oxides.
 
• Millions of tonnes of nitric acid are produced annually for use largely in fertilizer manufacture, with NO serving as an intermediary in this process.
 
• When the **temperature rises, the gas turns reddish-brown**.
 
• If inhaled in significant amounts, it can be **letha**l.
 
• A bent, **paramagnetic molecul**e with C2v point group symmetry is nitrogen dioxide.

questions.question: Ashoka appointed ______ to solve the social problems in his region.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**dhamma mahamatta**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• From 268 to 232 BCE, Ashoka appointed the **Dhamma Mahamatta. Around 260 B.C**.,
 
• He declared Buddhism the official religion.
 
• Also, he established a group of officials known as the dhamma-mahamattas, whose roles included both dhamma propagation and keeping the emperor abreast of public opinion.
 
• Religious practises that include the **sacrifice of animals **are practised.
 
• He hired a new group of officials called **Dhammamahamattas** to carry out his policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samaharta: **In ancient India, the samaharta was responsible for the collection of taxes and revenue from the people in a specific region.
 
• **Nyayadheesh: **Nyayadheesh refers to a judge or magistrate who presides over legal matters and ensures justice is served. 
 
• **Amatya:** Amatya refers to a minister or high-ranking official in ancient Indian administration.
